{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"PvP Solver","ApplicableVersion":"any","AssemblyVersion":"0.1.1.2","CategoryTags":null,"Changelog":"v0.1.2.3 (2026-10-18) [testing]
- **All 21 PvP rotations declare game version 7.57**, and their source-code metadata points to the current rotation paths.
- **Paladin Guardian uses only the configured general-ability checks.** Duplicate attack-ability triggers that could bypass the HP and Hallowed Ground settings are removed.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.2.2 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **When BossModReborn is unloaded, its timeline data (upcoming raidwides, tankbusters, knockbacks) is cleared once**, so proactive mitigation no longer acts on countdowns left over from before the unload.
- The last plugin lookup that could log an error on every call (the BossModReborn version lookup) reads the installed-plugin list instead.
- The BossModReborn check writes one log line when it first finds (or does not find) BossModReborn and one each time it is loaded or unloaded, never one per frame.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.2.1 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **BossModReborn integration was never detected, and it filled the log with errors.** The check for BossModReborn (and for WrathCombo) went through a lookup that cannot read BossModReborn's plugin object, so it reported the plugin as missing even while loaded, and wrote an error with a stack trace to the Dalamud log each time it was asked, once per frame while the settings window was open (over 11,000 lines in 35 minutes). The check now reads the list of installed plugins and quietly reports whether the plugin is loaded, so the BossModReborn timeline data is used when BossModReborn is running and the log stays clean.

v0.1.2.0 (2026-10-08) [testing]
- **New settings window.** `/pvpsolver`, the plugin's settings button and Lazy Hub now open a new window with the settings that matter for PvP, in plain words with a help line under each. It has six tabs: Match (when PvP Solver turns itself on and off), Survival (Guard, Purify, Sprint and the defensives master switch), Targeting (who to attack, area attacks, burst, invulnerable enemies), My Job, Display and Advanced.
- **Settings can be changed in any zone.** Every setting, including each job's own options, can be edited anywhere and for any of the 21 jobs, not only for the played job inside a PvP zone. Only turning PvP Solver on still needs a PvP zone; its button says so. Job options need a character in the world.
- **Optional automatic defensives, all off by default.** Each is a "use when HP is below" setting with its own percentage, per job, in the My Job tab: Aquaveil (White Mage), Wreath of Ice (Black Mage), Tempera Coat (Pictomancer), Forte (Red Mage), Radiant Aegis (Summoner), Arcane Crest (Reaper), Snake Scales (Viper), The Blackest Night (Dark Knight), Holy Sheltron (Paladin), Bloodwhetting (Warrior), Curing Waltz (Dancer), and the PvP role actions Rampart (tanks) and Stoneskin II (healers), which can be used only while they are the selected role action. Recuperate keeps its existing rule (15,000 or more HP missing) and gains an optional second condition, an HP percentage. Default percentages run from 45 to 70.
- **Defensives master switch.** One switch in the Survival tab (on by default) turns all automatic defensives off at once. It also covers the six that were already automatic at a fixed HP: Heart of Corundum, Riddle of Earth, Lady of Crowns, Microcosmos, Meisui and Impalement, so turning it off stops those too.
- **Worst case of the defensives.** After one automatic defensive is used no other is used for 2.5 seconds, and none while a barrier, damage reduction or heal of the same kind from another turned-on defensive is still active, but with several turned on, more than one can still be used during one long stretch of low HP.
- **Six fixed HP thresholds are now settings with unchanged defaults.** Heart of Corundum (Gunbreaker) at or below 30%, Riddle of Earth (Monk) below 80%, Lady of Crowns and Microcosmos (Astrologian) below 60%, Meisui (Ninja) below 50% and Impalement (Dark Knight) below 60% behave exactly as before until changed. Each can be moved or turned off in the My Job tab.

  /bocchi cmd flag-active-fate → Flag a FATE on the map
  /bocchi cmd flag-active-non-pot-fate → Flag a non-pot FATE
  /bocchi reload-translations → Reload translation files (alias: rt)

- A cute little Fate and CE panel that'll tell you what rewards it gives AND help you automatically path to it, wowee.
- An extra illegal 'illegal mode' for those of you that would rather be touching grass or playing a game with worthwhile content.

Command prefix: bocchi (alias: och)
  /bocchi → Opens the main window
  /bocchi config → Opens config (aliases: cfg, c)
  /bocchi config list → Lists config keys
  /bocchi config get <key> → Prints a config value
  /bocchi config set <key> <value> → Sets a config value
  /bocchi buff → Start/stop a buff run
  /bocchi tp [fate|ce|pot] → Teleport toward nearest matching activity
  /bocchi illegal [on|off|toggle] → Control Illegal Mode (no arg opens the window)
  /bocchi cmd flag-active-ce → Flag registering CE on the map
  /bocchi cmd flag-active-fate → Flag a FATE on the map
  /bocchi cmd flag-active-non-pot-fate → Flag a non-pot FATE
  /bocchi reload-translations → Reload translation files (alias: rt)
  /och … → Same as /bocchi (legacy alias; also /occultcrescenthelper)

Built for Occult Crescent and FATEs.","Changelog":"AutoRezzer now stands down completely in PvP - Frontline, Crystalline Conflict, Rival Wings and the Wolves' Den. Nothing sweeps, nothing swaps your job, and nothing accepts anything until you leave. Nobody can be raised in PvP, so there was never anything to gain in there, but there was plenty to lose: Frontline lets you change class at the spawn point, and the spawn point is exactly where dead players pile up waiting to respawn, so the plugin saw a field of bodies, decided an instant raise was called for, and turned you into a Red Mage mid-match - taking the damage you had done and your series progress on the class you queued as with it. {"Author":"Faye, Kage","Name":"Better Occult Crescent & Chest Helper Interface","InternalName":"BOCCHI","Punchline":"BOCCHI is here to smooth out your Occult Crescent experience.","Description":"BOCCHI is here to smooth out your Occult Crescent experience.

- A cute little Fate and CE panel that'll tell you what rewards it gives AND help you automatically path to it, wowee.
- An extra illegal 'illegal mode' for those of you that would rather be touching grass or playing a game with worthwhile content.

Command prefix: bocchi (alias: och)
  /bocchi → Opens the main window
  /bocchi config → Opens config (aliases: cfg, c)
  /bocchi config list → Lists config keys
  /bocchi config get <key> → Prints a config value
  /bocchi config set <key> <value> → Sets a config value
  /bocchi buff → Start/stop a buff run
  /bocchi tp [fate|ce|pot] → Teleport toward nearest matching activity
  /bocchi illegal [on|off|toggle] → Control Illegal Mode (no arg opens the window)
  /bocchi cmd flag-active-ce → Flag registering CE on the map
  /bocchi cmd flag-active-fate → Flag a FATE on the map
  /bocchi cmd flag-active-non-pot-fate → Flag a non-pot FATE
  /bocchi reload-translations → Reload translation files (alias: rt)
  /och … → Same as /bocchi (legacy alias; also /occultcrescenthelper)

{"Author":"Mayo Botic","Name":"Eureka Challenge Helper","InternalName":"EurekaChallengeHelper","AssemblyVersion":"0.1.0.0","Description":"Alpha.

Tracks the Eureka elemental challenge log while you play.

When you kill an enemy in Eureka that you get credit for, the plugin works out what it was - fire, ice, wind, earth, lightning or water aspected, a sprite, or an ashkin - and adds 1 to the matching counter, so your progress toward the weekly Elemental challenge log is always one banished glance away.

Every counter row also has a Track button. Switch it on and the plugin draws a line in the 3D view from your hitbox to every enemy that row would count, so you can find your ashkin or your fire aspected without having to target anything first. Element rows accept mobs up to two levels below you, sprites and ashkin must be your level or higher, exactly as the challenge log itself counts them.

Starting numbers: set them once in the window to match the current in-game log, use the +/- buttons, and hit the reset button when the week rolls over.

Enemy elements come from a bundled map of the four zones' enemies, and the aspect the game shows on a nameplate is picked up automatically. An enemy the plugin cannot place is not counted.

{"Author":"Faye, Kage","Name":"Better Occult Crescent & Chest Helper Interface","InternalName":"BOCCHI","Punchline":"BOCCHI is here to smooth out your Occult Crescent experience.","Description":"BOCCHI is here to smooth out your Occult Crescent experience.

- A cute little Fate and CE panel that'll tell you what rewards it gives AND help you automatically path to it, wowee.
- An extra illegal 'illegal mode' for those of you that would rather be touching grass or playing a game with worthwhile content.

Command prefix: bocchi (alias: och)
  /bocchi → Opens the main window
  /bocchi config → Opens config (aliases: cfg, c)
  /bocchi config list → Lists config keys
  /bocchi config get <key> → Prints a config value
  /bocchi config set <key> <value> → Sets a config value
  /bocchi buff → Start/stop a buff run
  /bocchi tp [fate|ce|pot] → Teleport toward nearest matching activity
  /bocchi illegal [on|off|toggle] → Control Illegal Mode (no arg opens the window)
  /bocchi cmd flag-active-ce → Flag registering CE on the map
  /bocchi cmd flag-active-fate → Flag a FATE on the map
  /bocchi cmd flag-active-non-pot-fate → Flag a non-pot FATE
  /bocchi reload-translations → Reload translation files (alias: rt)
  /och … → Same as /bocchi (legacy alias; also /occultcrescenthelper)

{"Author":"Mayo Botic","Name":"Eureka Challenge Helper","InternalName":"EurekaChallengeHelper","AssemblyVersion":"0.1.0.0","Description":"Alpha.

Tracks the Eureka elemental challenge log while you play.

When you kill an enemy in Eureka that you get credit for, the plugin works out what it was - fire, ice, wind, earth, lightning or water aspected, a sprite, or an ashkin - and adds 1 to the matching counter, so your progress toward the weekly Elemental challenge log is always one banished glance away.

Every counter row also has a Track button. Switch it on and the plugin draws a line in the 3D view from your hitbox to every enemy that row would count, so you can find your ashkin or your fire aspected without having to target anything first. Element rows accept mobs up to two levels below you, sprites and ashkin must be your level or higher, exactly as the challenge log itself counts them.

Starting numbers: set them once in the window to match the current in-game log, use the +/- buttons, and hit the reset button when the week rolls over.

Enemy elements come from a bundled map of the four zones' enemies, and the aspect the game shows on a nameplate is picked up automatically. An enemy the plugin cannot place is not counted.

{"Author":"Ice","Name":"Ice's Cosmic Exploration (ICE)","Punchline":"Welcome to, the dark side of, the MOOOON","Description":"The one-stop shop to your cosmic exploration needs! - Fisher can also be fully automated with the support of AutoHook and Navmesh

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"Gluttony Combo","Punchline":"Lalalazy fork of Wrath Combo - XIVCombo for very lazy players.","Description":"Gluttony Combo - lalalazy fork of Gluttony Combo. XIVCombo for very lazy players.","InternalName":"GluttonyCombo","AssemblyVersion":"1.0.4.301","Changelog":"v1.0.4.308 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- Telemetry only, no behaviour change: the Crucible decision log line (CR|) now carries the inputs the offline replay could not rebuild from the rest of the line - the target's invulnerability flag, the readiness of the Beastmaster's long cooldowns (the three horns, Shield Charge, Rally, Cheer, Beast Mode and the rest) as a bitmap, the health potion count, the player's current and maximum health, GCD and weave readiness, the in-combat and casting state, and whether Morphos or other enemies are still up. The offline replay tool reads these fields and replays the Crucible hold rules from them, so more of a recorded fight can be replayed faithfully.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.307 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- **Beastmaster in the Crucible of the Unbroken, King Ahriman Piece: the Final Hourglass is no longer broken at the moment that points the Death cone at the character.** Breaking the hourglass makes the needle fire Death, a 23-yard cone along the needle's heading at its next tick, and Death puts Doom on whatever stands in it: a 6-second countdown that ends in certain death and that no cleanse, dispel or item removes. The needle ticks every 1.56 seconds and turns a quarter turn after each tick, and the character stands bound beside the hourglass, so a break lands in the cone about one time in four. The recorded runs show it: Death hit the character in 6 of 12 roulettes and every Doom ended in death. The rotation used to break the hourglass as fast as possible whatever the needle did. Now, once the hourglass is low enough for a single hit to break it (75% of its health or less), the weaponskill is held whenever a needle tick that the break could precede points at the character, and goes out the moment none does; the needle points at the character a quarter of the time, so the wait is at most one turn of the needle (about 6 seconds). The hold gives up 12 seconds after the hourglass appears, and does nothing at all when the needle cannot be read, which leaves the previous behaviour.
- **The log records every turn of the needle (`NE|` lines: the needle's heading, the hourglass's health, the hourglass's age, and the character's bearing and distance from the needle).**
- Doom itself cannot be removed. The game marks the Crucible's Doom as not cleansable ("Certain death when counter reaches zero"): no beast action (Ultrasonics, Scouring Ash, Quelling Wave) and no Crucible item removes it, so the cleanse path correctly stays idle. Its Crucible sources are Mortal Ray and the Ahriman gaze (Taurus Piece; the lit floor tiles clear it), the Dirty Eye's Mortal Gaze (looking away avoids it) and the King Ahriman Piece's Death (fixed here); Soulreaper's Armor is the only item that resists Doom.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.306 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- **White Mage: Temperance and Divine Caress are now handled as the two separate actions they are.** Since the pair was split, the heal combos watched for the Divine Grace buff and pressed whatever Temperance had turned into. Now Temperance itself is used when it is ready - in the single-target, area and simple heal modes and in the raidwide features alike - and Divine Caress is pressed on its own when it is ready. The area-of-effect simple heal mode gains a Divine Caress step it did not have, and the Asylum replacement mode now tries Asylum first, then Temperance, then Divine Caress, instead of preferring Temperance while Asylum was on cooldown.
- **A ground-placed action is no longer fired before it is ready.** The action watcher could send a ground-target placement for a replacement action that was still on cooldown; it now checks readiness first.
- Merges upstream WrathCombo changes through 2026-10-14 (9 commits). The automatic regen and shield checks on the focus target now use the plugin's own status lookup, ending an ambiguity with the shared library's lookup of the same name.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.305 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- **Beastmaster in the Crucible of the Unbroken, Abaddon Piece: the rotation no longer stands idle while a Morpho is alive.** The Abaddon was held back from the start of the fight until every Morpho was gone, and the Morphos themselves are never attacked, so for as long as a Morpho lived (over a minute in a recorded fight) the Abaddon was the only enemy and nothing was left that the rotation was allowed to hit: no damage and no aggro while the Morphos confused the character. Intended behaviour in this piece: the Drake and the Barbmoles are killed first, as before; once the Abaddon is the only enemy left it is attacked and chipped down to 35% of its health, and held there while any Morpho is alive, so it is never killed ahead of the Morphos it feeds on; once the last Morpho is gone it is attacked to the end. Eggs and Morphos as targets are still never attacked, and the Gigantis gel rule is unchanged.
- The Abaddon's Regen (Rehabilitation, one minute, renewed each time it eats a Morpho) is deliberately not dispelled: Quelling Wave never removed it in the recorded casts (15 casts on the Abaddon, the buff always ran its full minute), so the rotation does not spend casts on it. The Drake's Blaze Spikes are still dispelled.

v1.0.4.307 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- **Beastmaster in the Crucible of the Unbroken, King Ahriman Piece: the Final Hourglass is no longer broken at the moment that points the Death cone at the character.** Breaking the hourglass makes the needle fire Death, a 23-yard cone along the needle's heading at its next tick, and Death puts Doom on whatever stands in it: a 6-second countdown that ends in certain death and that no cleanse, dispel or item removes. The needle ticks every 1.56 seconds and turns a quarter turn after each tick, and the character stands bound beside the hourglass, so a break lands in the cone about one time in four. The recorded runs show it: Death hit the character in 6 of 12 roulettes and every Doom ended in death. The rotation used to break the hourglass as fast as possible whatever the needle did. Now, once the hourglass is low enough for a single hit to break it (75% of its health or less), the weaponskill is held whenever a needle tick that the break could precede points at the character, and goes out the moment none does; the needle points at the character a quarter of the time, so the wait is at most one turn of the needle (about 6 seconds). The hold gives up 12 seconds after the hourglass appears, and does nothing at all when the needle cannot be read, which leaves the previous behaviour.
- **The log records every turn of the needle (`NE|` lines: the needle's heading, the hourglass's health, the hourglass's age, and the character's bearing and distance from the needle).**
- Doom itself cannot be removed. Its Crucible sources are Mortal Ray and the Ahriman gaze (Taurus Piece; the lit floor tiles clear it), the Dirty Eye's Mortal Gaze (looking away avoids it) and the King Ahriman Piece's Death (fixed here); Soulreaper's Armor is the only item that resists Doom.

- **Switches and settings for the whole suite.** Plugins that offer controls can be turned on or off and have their common settings changed from the hub, over Dalamud IPC. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the owning plugin's own window does; the hub never writes another plugin's configuration.
- **Quick tab:** a Gluttony Combo tray with the Auto-Rotation switch and hotbar buttons (click a button, then click a hotbar slot to place the action; Escape cancels), then one switch per plugin that offers one. Switches with real consequences (Auto-Market, the FATE bot) ask for a second click within a few seconds.
- **Plugin page:** the plugin's settings in groups: switches, number steppers (`-` and `+`) and option pickers (`<` and `>`). A setting that another plugin or a running task holds is shown as locked with the reason and refuses changes.
- **Plugins tab:** all fifteen plugins with status, Settings and Open. A plugin on a version that does not offer controls yet has Open only.
- **Safe mode:** `/lazy safe` switches to the plain window and back. The choice is remembered.
- **Look:** the window frame is tinted toward lalalazy green with forest-green panels, gold accents and each plugin's icon.

- **Plugin icons fit their slot.** They were drawn at their full 64-pixel size instead of the 44-pixel slot, which covered the first letters of each name and status line and touched the row below.

- Testing channel only. Plugins offer controls from the versions released with this one: update them to see their settings here.
- The hub asks each plugin for its controls about once a second while the window is open and not at all while it is closed.
- After an update the "What's new" window shows these notes once. `/lazy changelog` reopens them.

v0.1.0.0 (2026-10-03)

- **First release: one in-game window for the whole lalalazy suite.** `/lazy` (or `/lazyhub`) opens a native game-style window with two tabs.
- **Plugins tab:** all fifteen lalalazy plugins in a grid, each with its icon, its name, a live status and an Open button. Status reads as Loaded, Loaded (testing), Not loaded or Not installed, and refreshes about once a second. Open launches that plugin's main window (or its settings window when it has no main window) and is available only while the plugin is running.
- **Quick tab:** shows whether Gluttony Combo's auto-rotation is on or off, read from Gluttony Combo itself. The card says so when Gluttony Combo is not running.
- **Server info bar entry** showing how many of the suite's plugins are running, for example `13/15`. Clicking it opens or closes the window.
- The plugin opens from the Dalamud plugin installer's Open button as well.

- This is a testing-channel first release. It reads status and opens windows; it does not change any plugin's settings yet.
- The window uses the stock game window frame. The icons are the repository's pixel-art plugin icons.

- Fixed a rare game crash when the plugin updates while the game is running: while its hooks are active and the plugin is updated again, they are disabled only after any call still inside them has finished, so a call can no longer land on a hook that is already gone. - Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v3.2.3.1 (2026-09-07)

- Removed the `/lazywtmath` command introduced in 3.2.3.0. It existed only to reopen the "What's new" popup, and this plugin's only interface is the probability readout inside the Wondrous Tails window itself.
- The changelog popup itself is unchanged: it still opens once automatically after an update, and it can be reopened any time from the Dalamud plugin installer (the plugin's "Open" button).
- No math, plugin behaviour or configuration changed.

v3.2.3.0 (2026-09-05)

- Added the in-game "What's new" popup. After Lazy WT Math updates, its changelog now opens once inside the game so the changes are visible without a trip to GitHub. It waits until the character is logged in and out of combat, duty, cutscenes and zoning; closing it (Got it, X or Escape) marks it read.
- New command `/lazywtmath` reopens that popup. This plugin had no command at all before: the probabilities still appear inside the Wondrous Tails window itself, exactly as before, and nothing about how they are calculated has changed.
- The rebuild against current FFXIVClientStructs from 3.2.2.10 (which stopped the Wondrous Tails crash loop) is included.

v3.2.2.10 - 2026-09-05
- **Rebuilt against current FFXIVClientStructs (7.55.1.8875) to stop the WeeklyBingo crash loop.** The 3.2.2.9 binaries (built 2026-07-02) threw `System.TypeLoadException: Could not load type 'FFXIVClientStructs.FFXIV.Client.System.Memory.ICreatable'` from `AddonWeeklyBingoController.AddonRefresh` on every WeeklyBingo PostUpdate (3,032 errors in one session on 2026-09-05), because the bundled KamiToolKit.dll was compiled against an older FFXIVClientStructs whose `ICreatable<T>` shape no longer matches the one Dalamud ships. No source changes; clean Release rebuild of LazyWTMath + KamiToolKit against the Dalamud 15.0.3.2 hooks currently loading in the client (files: `KamiToolKit.dll`, `LazyWTMath.dll`).

- Fix for Helm thread t-plugerr-52f9741c16e8 (kanban t_a7838408). If the crash persists after updating, the next step is merging upstream MidoriKami/EzWondrousTails and its current KamiToolKit.

v3.2.2.9 - 2026-07-02
- **Plugin icon now shows in the Dalamud installer.** Installed copies were built before

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"AutoPotion","Punchline":"Per-job HP, MP, and deep dungeon potion automation.","Description":"Auto-uses the highest-tier HP potion, MP potion (Ether), and the deep dungeon regen potion (Sustaining / Eurekan / Orthos / Pilgrim's) at configurable thresholds. Each potion's threshold and on/off state is stored per-job, so casters and tanks can have completely different setups.","InternalName":"AutoPotion","AssemblyVersion":"0.2.5.2","Changelog":"v0.2.5.2 (2026-10-10) [testing]
- **Automatic item uses no longer cancel an open action sequence.** Any potion, ether, deep dungeon medicine or Echo Drops that would land while mudra seals or Ten Chi Jin are held is delayed until the sequence completes, instead of cancelling the ninjutsu mid-chain. The delay lasts only while the sequence is up (a mudra window is about six seconds) and lifts immediately after; at or below 25% HP the heal fires regardless - a cancelled jutsu is cheaper than dying. No other job's behaviour changes.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- With the optional decision log enabled, a held use is recorded with the `heldmudra` near-miss reason, rate-limited like every other near-miss line.

v0.2.5.1 (2026-10-03) [testing]
- **Quick controls for the Lazy Hub window.** The plugin now offers the master switch, "Only in combat", "Only in a duty", the HP, MP and Regen potion switches with their thresholds, and Cure Silence (Echo Drops) to Lazy Hub (`/lazy`) over Dalamud IPC, so they can be changed from one window next to the other lalalazy plugins. Each change does exactly what the matching setting in the plugin's own window does.
- The potion settings apply to the active job's profile, as in the settings window.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
- Without Lazy Hub installed the plugin behaves exactly as before.

v0.2.5.0 (2026-09-05)

- New per-job option: "Auto-use Echo Drops when silenced". When it is on and Silence lands (mob silence spells, AoE silences, deep dungeon traps), AutoPotion uses Echo Drops from inventory to cure it automatically. Item use is not blocked by Silence, so the cure works exactly when nothing else can.
- OFF by default like every option, and per job like the rest: tick the new box in the settings window for the jobs it should apply to. With it off (the default) nothing changes - not even a status check.
- It reuses the same machinery as the potions: HQ Echo Drops are preferred over normal ones, the shared 750 ms cooldown after any potion use applies, and a Silence that arrives during that cooldown is cured on the next tick.
- If the diagnostic tap is enabled, the cure logs as an `e` event; when it cannot fire the near-miss reasons are `edblocked` (on cooldown / blocked) or `ednostock` (none in the bags).
- No change to potion behaviour. HP/MP/regen thresholds, the overshoot guard, the deep dungeon Rehabilitation lockout and the in-combat / in-duty gates all work exactly as before.

v0.2.4.0 (2026-09-05)

- Added an optional "Log potion decisions" diagnostic, OFF by default. Turn it on with `/autopotion telemetry on` or the new Advanced / Diagnostics section of the settings window, and AutoPotion writes one line to its plugin log every time it uses a potion, plus a rate-limited line when a threshold was crossed and nothing fired.
- Purpose: the log line records the HP%, the MP%, the threshold that was in force and the job, so a threshold can be verified after the fact instead of guessed at. Nothing leaves the machine - the lines only go to the local Dalamud plugin log.
- The "nothing fired" lines say WHY in a short code: `hpover` (a potion was available but the heal would have been wasted), `hpblocked` / `mpblocked` / `rgblocked` (on cooldown or blocked by a status), `hpnostock` / `mpnostock` / `rgnostock` (none left in inventory) and `rgrehab` (Rehabilitation still up in a deep dungeon).
- These lines are heavily rate-limited on purpose: a repeated state logs once, not once per frame. Measured against 214 minutes of real play the near-miss lines come out under one line per minute, so the log stays readable.
- No change to potion behaviour. Thresholds, per-job profiles, the overshoot guard, the deep dungeon Rehabilitation lockout and the in-combat / in-duty gates all work exactly as before, and with the setting off (the default) the plugin does not even build a log line.

v0.2.3.0 (2026-09-05)

- Added the in-game "What's new" popup. After AutoPotion updates, its changelog now opens once inside the game so the changes are visible without a trip to GitHub. It waits until the character is logged in and out of combat, duty, cutscenes and zoning; closing it (Got it, X or Escape) marks it read. Type `/autopotion changelog` any time to reopen it.
- No change to potion behaviour: thresholds, per-job profiles and the in-combat / in-duty gates all work exactly as before.

{"Author":"Faye, Kage","Name":"Better Occult Crescent & Chest Helper Interface","InternalName":"BOCCHI","Punchline":"BOCCHI is here to smooth out your Occult Crescent experience.","Description":"BOCCHI is here to smooth out your Occult Crescent experience.
- No more of that pesky 'walking' or 'finding chests'. That's for losers.
- A cute little Fate and CE panel that'll tell you what rewards it gives AND help you automatically path to it, wowee.
- An extra illegal 'illegal mode' for those of you that would rather be touching grass or playing a game with worthwhile content.

{"Author":"Valenth Siveria","Name":"I Am Ready","Punchline":"Automatically accept or decline Duty Finder ready checks based on a configurable counter.","Description":"# I Am Ready

**I Am Ready** is a Dalamud plugin for Final Fantasy XIV that automatically accepts or declines Party and Alliance Ready Checks based on a customizable counter. 

Whether you are stepping away for a moment or just tired of clicking, this plugin handles ready checks for you while mimicking human reaction times.

## ✨ Features

* **Auto-Answer Ready Checks:** Automatically clicks "Yes" or "No" when a ready check appears.
* **Configurable "Yes" Counter:** Set a specific number of times you want to automatically answer "Yes". Once that limit is reached, the plugin will automatically start answering "No" to prevent pulling when you are actually away.
* **Natural Delay:** Enable a randomized delay (0.7 to 2.5 seconds) before the plugin answers, making it look like a natural human reaction.
* **Smart Chat Triggers (Regex):** Add custom text phrases to the plugin. If someone says one of these phrases in Party or Alliance chat (e.g., "reset", "pulling"), your counter will automatically reset back to zero.
* **Bilingual Support:** The user interface is available in both English and German.

## 🚀 Usage

1. Type `/iar` in the in-game chat to open the configuration window.
2. Click the **Inactive/Active** button at the top to turn the auto-responder on or off.
3. Adjust the **Yes Count** slider. For example, if set to `5`, the plugin will answer "Yes" to the next 5 ready checks, and "No" to any checks after that.
4. Click the **Start** button at any time to manually reset your current counter back to zero.

### Chat Triggers (Regex Patterns)
At the bottom of the window, you can expand the **Regex Patterns** section. Here you can add simple words or complex regex patterns. 
If the plugin reads a matching message in your Party or Cross-World Party chat, it will instantly reset your counter to zero, assuming a new pull or instance is starting!

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"LazyCrucible","Punchline":"Crucible of the Unbroken familiar picks, filled in for every fight","Description":"For the Beastmaster duty Crucible of the Unbroken. Fills the ten-familiar run roster at the Bentbranch Meadows entry menu and the three Battlehorn slots before every fight with the familiars that answer that fight's mechanics: elemental weakness, interrupts, dispels, cleanses and crowd control, skipping knocked-out familiars and benching badly hurt ones. Picks are announced in chat. Every automation has its own toggle and manual edits always win. Includes the beast-pick advisor for every board and a read-only recorder that writes each Crucible screen to the Dalamud log. Use /lazycrucible to open.","InternalName":"LazyCrucible","AssemblyVersion":"0.1.9.5","TestingAssemblyVersion":"0.1.9.16","TestingDalamudApiLevel":15,"Changelog":"v0.1.9.16 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **"Score: three familiars" run-roster mode, off by default.** For score runs. A run roster of one to three familiars scores the Beast Squad III bonus on every board, so with the option on the run roster is the best three familiars for the whole board instead of the board's full roster. The three are chosen from the familiars you own and that are not knocked out: they cover as many of the board's required interrupt, dispel and cleanse needs as any three can, then the damage the board calls to be blunted, then three of one kin when that costs no required cover (the Gambit bonus), then the rest by points. A roster of three saved for a different board is rewritten for the board you enter. Whatever the three cannot answer on the board is named on the window's summary line; nothing pops up. With three or fewer familiars the game registers the battlehorns itself, so the plugin leaves them alone. Found in the settings window and the Lazy Hub as "Score: three familiars".
- With the option off, nothing changes. While AutoDuty drives the run roster the plugin stands by there, option on or off.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.9.15 (2026-10-13) [testing]
- **Mitigation in the horn picks.** Fights with a damage wall now field a familiar that blunts it, ranked below every interrupt, dispel and cleanse need, and counted only for a familiar above the danger HP line. Durga's Atomic Ray gets a magic answer (drake's Smoldering Scales, pugil's Water Wall or a Scalekin's Scaleskin); Borgny gets coblyn's Vulcanize for the poison plus a magic answer; Gargoyle's Sweeping Evisceration gets a physical answer (a Beastkin's Beastskin, coblyn's Vulcanize or adamantoise's Harden Shell). The fight guide lists these under "Calls for".
- One telemetry line per fight names the team on the horns and the needs it cannot answer (`uncovered=`).
- **Works with AutoDuty.** While AutoDuty runs, it handles the run roster, shop, treasure, spoils and campsite itself, so the plugin stands by there; the battlehorns are AutoDuty's only with its "Fight picks" on, and the plugin picks them otherwise. AutoDuty's active profile is read through AutoDuty's own interface (its config file when that is unavailable), never changed; when neither can be read, every screen stands by, as before. The window shows one quiet line naming the screens it is standing by on.
- **No more corrections on top of AutoDuty's familiar picks.** AutoDuty re-applied its own picks every time, so they never reached a fight.
- **Fight guide: the Snarl -> Parting Blow advice is gone** (Parting Blow no longer dodges a hit since the September 17 hotfix). Plain tankbusters say to let a familiar with enough HP take them under Snarl; poisoning ones (Deadly Thrust, Cold Caress, Toxic Vomit) say to Parting Blow right after the hit so the poison leaves with the familiar; Gargoyle's Sweeping Evisceration says to save the Blink tome for it.
- Item values: Beastly Knife is valued like the elemental axes; Hero's Crown counts its Excellence proc (9 s of nullified attacks); Rapid Recast gear is valued; reraise items are worth a little less at Third Degree.
- **Patch 7.57: battlehorns the game registered itself (teams of three or fewer) are left alone**; a knocked-out member of a three-familiar team is no longer toggled off the horns.
- **Patch 7.57: the board's degree survives a job change** (the game now keeps the Crucible Mode until logout), so the degree passed to Gluttony Combo is no longer reset when the character returns to Beastmaster. It is forgotten at logout.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v0.1.9.14 (2026-10-06) [testing]
- **The board's difficulty degree now reaches Gluttony Combo during a fight.** The degree is set in the lobby (by a click or by AutoDuty) and the character then zones into the duty; the plugin used to forget it at every loading screen, so a fight always read as an unknown degree. It is now kept across loading screens and still forgotten when the Beastmaster job is left or the plugin unloads.

v0.1.9.13 (2026-10-06) [testing]
- **The board's difficulty degree is now read and shared with Gluttony Combo.** The Crucible board layout reports the degree whenever it is set, by a click or by AutoDuty; the plugin keeps the last one (Standard, First, Second or Third) and offers it to Gluttony Combo 1.0.4.288 or newer, which uses it to price the hits a familiar or the character will take. The degree is forgotten when the Beastmaster job is left, and until the first time it is set the plugin reports none. The change is logged as one `PS|` line (`note=degree`).
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.9.12 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- **The run-roster need-coverage correction no longer fires while AutoDuty drives the screen.** AutoDuty re-asserts its own roster through a confirm sequence that removes unfamiliar rows one per pass and holds its acceptance until they are gone; every correction written on that surface was removed before entry, and the acceptance follows the build's last pick by about half a second with nothing the plugin can observe in between — a guess there only spent the correction budget on rows that were going to be removed anyway. The surface is now left to AutoDuty entirely. The battlehorn surface is unchanged.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.

v0.1.9.11 (2026-10-05) [testing]
- **The run-roster need-coverage correction now waits for the roster itself to stop changing.** The previous fix judged a settled roster by edit timestamps, but the roster AutoDuty builds is driven through the monster notebook, whose selection writes never register as edits — so the timestamp stayed at screen-open while the build was still adding picks, and the correction still fired mid-build, where AutoDuty's continuing build and its confirm passes removed the added rows. The correction is now due only once the selected roster has been unchanged for 1.5 seconds — what the plugin sees every frame — never on an empty roster, and it still re-arms after any later AutoDuty write. The screen log's roster needfix line now also carries the age of the last edit (`adedit=`), the roster's quiet time (`adstb=`) and the selected count (`flutes=`).
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.","RepoUrl":"https://github.com/dajoey/lalalazy/tree/main/src/LazyCrucible","ApplicableVersion":"any","DalamudApiLevel":15,"IsHide":false,"IsTestingExclusive":false,"DownloadLinkInstall":"https://github.com/dajoey/lalalazy/releases/download/LazyCrucible-v0.1.9.5/LazyCrucible.zip","DownloadLinkUpdate":"https://github.com/dajoey/lalalazy/releases/download/LazyCrucible-v0.1.9.5/LazyCrucible.zip","DownloadLinkTesting":"https://github.com/dajoey/lalalazy/releases/download/LazyCrucible-v0.1.9.16/LazyCrucible-testing.zip","Tags":["beastmaster","bst","crucible","unbroken","familiar","battlehorn","automation"],"CategoryTags":["jobs","utility"],"IconUrl":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dajoey/lalalazy/main/LalaImages/lazycrucible-icon.png","ImageUrls":[""],"DownloadCount":0,"LastUpdate":"0","_SourceId":"dajoey-lalalazy","_SourceName":"dajoey / lalalazy","_SourceUrl":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dajoey/lalalazy/main/pluginmaster.json","_Category":"automation"}

{"Author":"Faye, Kage","Name":"Better Occult Crescent & Chest Helper Interface","InternalName":"BOCCHI","Punchline":"BOCCHI is here to smooth out your Occult Crescent experience.","Description":"BOCCHI is here to smooth out your Occult Crescent experience.

- An extra illegal 'illegal mode' for those of you that would rather be touching grass or playing a game with worthwhile content.

Command prefix: bocchi (alias: och)
  /bocchi → Opens the main window
  /bocchi config → Opens config (aliases: cfg, c)
  /bocchi config list → Lists config keys
  /bocchi config get <key> → Prints a config value
  /bocchi config set <key> <value> → Sets a config value
  /bocchi buff → Start/stop a buff run
  /bocchi tp [fate|ce|pot] → Teleport toward nearest matching activity
  /bocchi illegal [on|off|toggle] → Control Illegal Mode (no arg opens the window)
  /bocchi cmd flag-active-ce → Flag registering CE on the map
  /bocchi cmd flag-active-fate → Flag a FATE on the map
  /bocchi cmd flag-active-non-pot-fate → Flag a non-pot FATE

XIVCombo for very lazy players.","InternalName":"GluttonyCombo","AssemblyVersion":"1.0.4.301","Changelog":"v1.0.4.308 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- Telemetry only, no behaviour change: the Crucible decision log line (CR|) now carries the inputs the offline replay could not rebuild from the rest of the line - the target's invulnerability flag, the readiness of the Beastmaster's long cooldowns (the three horns, Shield Charge, Rally, Cheer, Beast Mode and the rest) as a bitmap, the health potion count, the player's current and maximum health, GCD and weave readiness, the in-combat and casting state, and whether Morphos or other enemies are still up. The offline replay tool reads these fields and replays the Crucible hold rules from them, so more of a recorded fight can be replayed faithfully.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.307 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- **Beastmaster in the Crucible of the Unbroken, King Ahriman Piece: the Final Hourglass is no longer broken at the moment that points the Death cone at the character.** Breaking the hourglass makes the needle fire Death, a 23-yard cone along the needle's heading at its next tick, and Death puts Doom on whatever stands in it: a 6-second countdown that ends in certain death and that no cleanse, dispel or item removes. The needle ticks every 1.56 seconds and turns a quarter turn after each tick, and the character stands bound beside the hourglass, so a break lands in the cone about one time in four. The recorded runs show it: Death hit the character in 6 of 12 roulettes and every Doom ended in death. The rotation used to break the hourglass as fast as possible whatever the needle did. Now, once the hourglass is low enough for a single hit to break it (75% of its health or less), the weaponskill is held whenever a needle tick that the break could precede points at the character, and goes out the moment none does; the needle points at the character a quarter of the time, so the wait is at most one turn of the needle (about 6 seconds). The hold gives up 12 seconds after the hourglass appears, and does nothing at all when the needle cannot be read, which leaves the previous behaviour.
- **The log records every turn of the needle (`NE|` lines: the needle's heading, the hourglass's health, the hourglass's age, and the character's bearing and distance from the needle).**
- Doom itself cannot be removed. The game marks the Crucible's Doom as not cleansable ("Certain death when counter reaches zero"): no beast action (Ultrasonics, Scouring Ash, Quelling Wave) and no Crucible item removes it, so the cleanse path correctly stays idle. Its Crucible sources are Mortal Ray and the Ahriman gaze (Taurus Piece; the lit floor tiles clear it), the Dirty Eye's Mortal Gaze (looking away avoids it) and the King Ahriman Piece's Death (fixed here); Soulreaper's Armor is the only item that resists Doom.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.306 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- **White Mage: Temperance and Divine Caress are now handled as the two separate actions they are.** Since the pair was split, the heal combos watched for the Divine Grace buff and pressed whatever Temperance had turned into. Now Temperance itself is used when it is ready - in the single-target, area and simple heal modes and in the raidwide features alike - and Divine Caress is pressed on its own when it is ready. The area-of-effect simple heal mode gains a Divine Caress step it did not have, and the Asylum replacement mode now tries Asylum first, then Temperance, then Divine Caress, instead of preferring Temperance while Asylum was on cooldown.
- **A ground-placed action is no longer fired before it is ready.** The action watcher could send a ground-target placement for a replacement action that was still on cooldown; it now checks readiness first.
- Merges upstream WrathCombo changes through 2026-10-14 (9 commits). The automatic regen and shield checks on the focus target now use the plugin's own status lookup, ending an ambiguity with the shared library's lookup of the same name.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.305 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- **Beastmaster in the Crucible of the Unbroken, Abaddon Piece: the rotation no longer stands idle while a Morpho is alive.** The Abaddon was held back from the start of the fight until every Morpho was gone, and the Morphos themselves are never attacked, so for as long as a Morpho lived (over a minute in a recorded fight) the Abaddon was the only enemy and nothing was left that the rotation was allowed to hit: no damage and no aggro while the Morphos confused the character. Intended behaviour in this piece: the Drake and the Barbmoles are killed first, as before; once the Abaddon is the only enemy left it is attacked and chipped down to 35% of its health, and held there while any Morpho is alive, so it is never killed ahead of the Morphos it feeds on; once the last Morpho is gone it is attacked to the end. Eggs and Morphos as targets are still never attacked, and the Gigantis gel rule is unchanged.
- The Abaddon's Regen (Rehabilitation, one minute, renewed each time it eats a Morpho) is deliberately not dispelled: Quelling Wave never removed it in the recorded casts (15 casts on the Abaddon, the buff always ran its full minute), so the rotation does not spend casts on it. The Drake's Blaze Spikes are still dispelled.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.304 (2026-10-14) [testing]
- **While another plugin controls the rotation, a training dummy that is the chosen target is left alone too.** The Manual mode, the manual area-of-effect aim and the Tank Target mode take their target from a selected target - the character's own, or in Tank Target mode the tank's - instead of from the enemy filter that 1.0.4.303 added, so a Striking Dummy that was already selected could still be struck while a lease was held. The same dummy check now covers that path: while another plugin is in control or still holds a lease, the dummy is not attacked even as the chosen target; without a lease the player's own choice stands.
- The external-control check reads the lease table directly on every tick instead of building a list for each read (the rotation consults it several times a tick).
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.303 (2026-10-14) [testing]
- **Another plugin driving the rotation (AutoDuty and the like) no longer attacks a training dummy, and no longer keeps control after it has stopped.** A training dummy never dies, so a first hit pulled out of combat held the character in combat with it, and the rotation then went on hitting it even after external control had ended. Now, while another plugin controls the rotation or still holds a lease on it, the Striking Dummy is not picked as an enemy at all. External control also does not apply in cities, inns and housing districts or their interiors, so a plugin that walks through one cannot start a fight there. AutoDuty re-asserts the rotation every 5 seconds during a run and goes silent between runs without releasing it, so it now counts as in control for one minute after its last call instead of ten; other plugins keep the ten-minute window. Every job is covered: the checks sit in the shared auto-rotation gate, not in any job's combo.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. - **Beastmaster in the Crucible of the Unbroken, King Ahriman Piece: the Final Hourglass is no longer broken at the moment that points the Death cone at the character.** Breaking the hourglass makes the needle fire Death, a 23-yard cone along the needle's heading at its next tick, and Death puts Doom on whatever stands in it: a 6-second countdown that ends in certain death and that no cleanse, dispel or item removes. The needle ticks every 1.56 seconds and turns a quarter turn after each tick, and the character stands bound beside the hourglass, so a break lands in the cone about one time in four. The recorded runs show it: Death hit the character in 6 of 12 roulettes and every Doom ended in death. The rotation used to break the hourglass as fast as possible whatever the needle did. Now, once the hourglass is low enough for a single hit to break it (75% of its health or less), the weaponskill is held whenever a needle tick that the break could precede points at the character, and goes out the moment none does; the needle points at the character a quarter of the time, so the wait is at most one turn of the needle (about 6 seconds). The hold gives up 12 seconds after the hourglass appears, and does nothing at all when the needle cannot be read, which leaves the previous behaviour.
- **The log records every turn of the needle (`NE|` lines: the needle's heading, the hourglass's health, the hourglass's age, and the character's bearing and distance from the needle).**
- Doom itself cannot be removed. The game marks the Crucible's Doom as not cleansable ("Certain death when counter reaches zero"): no beast action (Ultrasonics, Scouring Ash, Quelling Wave) and no Crucible item removes it, so the cleanse path correctly stays idle. Its Crucible sources are Mortal Ray and the Ahriman gaze (Taurus Piece; the lit floor tiles clear it), the Dirty Eye's Mortal Gaze (looking away avoids it) and the King Ahriman Piece's Death (fixed here); Soulreaper's Armor is the only item that resists Doom.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.306 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- **White Mage: Temperance and Divine Caress are now handled as the two separate actions they are.** Since the pair was split, the heal combos watched for the Divine Grace buff and pressed whatever Temperance had turned into. Now Temperance itself is used when it is ready - in the single-target, area and simple heal modes and in the raidwide features alike - and Divine Caress is pressed on its own when it is ready. The area-of-effect simple heal mode gains a Divine Caress step it did not have, and the Asylum replacement mode now tries Asylum first, then Temperance, then Divine Caress, instead of preferring Temperance while Asylum was on cooldown.
- **A ground-placed action is no longer fired before it is ready.** The action watcher could send a ground-target placement for a replacement action that was still on cooldown; it now checks readiness first.
- Merges upstream WrathCombo changes through 2026-10-14 (9 commits). The automatic regen and shield checks on the focus target now use the plugin's own status lookup, ending an ambiguity with the shared library's lookup of the same name.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.305 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- **Beastmaster in the Crucible of the Unbroken, Abaddon Piece: the rotation no longer stands idle while a Morpho is alive.** The Abaddon was held back from the start of the fight until every Morpho was gone, and the Morphos themselves are never attacked, so for as long as a Morpho lived (over a minute in a recorded fight) the Abaddon was the only enemy and nothing was left that the rotation was allowed to hit: no damage and no aggro while the Morphos confused the character. Intended behaviour in this piece: the Drake and the Barbmoles are killed first, as before; once the Abaddon is the only enemy left it is attacked and chipped down to 35% of its health, and held there while any Morpho is alive, so it is never killed ahead of the Morphos it feeds on; once the last Morpho is gone it is attacked to the end. Eggs and Morphos as targets are still never attacked, and the Gigantis gel rule is unchanged.
- The Abaddon's Regen (Rehabilitation, one minute, renewed each time it eats a Morpho) is deliberately not dispelled: Quelling Wave never removed it in the recorded casts (15 casts on the Abaddon, the buff always ran its full minute), so the rotation does not spend casts on it. The Drake's Blaze Spikes are still dispelled.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.304 (2026-10-14) [testing]
- **While another plugin controls the rotation, a training dummy that is the chosen target is left alone too.** The Manual mode, the manual area-of-effect aim and the Tank Target mode take their target from a selected target - the character's own, or in Tank Target mode the tank's - instead of from the enemy filter that 1.0.4.303 added, so a Striking Dummy that was already selected could still be struck while a lease was held. The same dummy check now covers that path: while another plugin is in control or still holds a lease, the dummy is not attacked even as the chosen target; without a lease the player's own choice stands.
- The external-control check reads the lease table directly on every tick instead of building a list for each read (the rotation consults it several times a tick).
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.303 (2026-10-14) [testing]
- **Another plugin driving the rotation (AutoDuty and the like) no longer attacks a training dummy, and no longer keeps control after it has stopped.** A training dummy never dies, so a first hit pulled out of combat held the character in combat with it, and the rotation then went on hitting it even after external control had ended. Now, while another plugin controls the rotation or still holds a lease on it, the Striking Dummy is not picked as an enemy at all. External control also does not apply in cities, inns and housing districts or their interiors, so a plugin that walks through one cannot start a fight there. AutoDuty re-asserts the rotation every 5 seconds during a run and goes silent between runs without releasing it, so it now counts as in control for one minute after its last call instead of ten; other plugins keep the ten-minute window. Every job is covered: the checks sit in the shared auto-rotation gate, not in any job's combo.

{"Author":"dajoey","Name":"Gluttony Combo","Punchline":"Lalalazy fork of Wrath Combo - XIVCombo for very lazy players.","Description":"Gluttony Combo - lalalazy fork of Gluttony Combo. XIVCombo for very lazy players.","InternalName":"GluttonyCombo","AssemblyVersion":"1.0.4.301","Changelog":"v1.0.4.308 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- Telemetry only, no behaviour change: the Crucible decision log line (CR|) now carries the inputs the offline replay could not rebuild from the rest of the line - the target's invulnerability flag, the readiness of the Beastmaster's long cooldowns (the three horns, Shield Charge, Rally, Cheer, Beast Mode and the rest) as a bitmap, the health potion count, the player's current and maximum health, GCD and weave readiness, the in-combat and casting state, and whether Morphos or other enemies are still up. The offline replay tool reads these fields and replays the Crucible hold rules from them, so more of a recorded fight can be replayed faithfully.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.307 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- **Beastmaster in the Crucible of the Unbroken, King Ahriman Piece: the Final Hourglass is no longer broken at the moment that points the Death cone at the character.** Breaking the hourglass makes the needle fire Death, a 23-yard cone along the needle's heading at its next tick, and Death puts Doom on whatever stands in it: a 6-second countdown that ends in certain death and that no cleanse, dispel or item removes. The needle ticks every 1.56 seconds and turns a quarter turn after each tick, and the character stands bound beside the hourglass, so a break lands in the cone about one time in four. The recorded runs show it: Death hit the character in 6 of 12 roulettes and every Doom ended in death. The rotation used to break the hourglass as fast as possible whatever the needle did. Now, once the hourglass is low enough for a single hit to break it (75% of its health or less), the weaponskill is held whenever a needle tick that the break could precede points at the character, and goes out the moment none does; the needle points at the character a quarter of the time, so the wait is at most one turn of the needle (about 6 seconds). The hold gives up 12 seconds after the hourglass appears, and does nothing at all when the needle cannot be read, which leaves the previous behaviour.
- **The log records every turn of the needle (`NE|` lines: the needle's heading, the hourglass's health, the hourglass's age, and the character's bearing and distance from the needle).**
- Doom itself cannot be removed. The game marks the Crucible's Doom as not cleansable ("Certain death when counter reaches zero"): no beast action (Ultrasonics, Scouring Ash, Quelling Wave) and no Crucible item removes it, so the cleanse path correctly stays idle. Its Crucible sources are Mortal Ray and the Ahriman gaze (Taurus Piece; the lit floor tiles clear it), the Dirty Eye's Mortal Gaze (looking away avoids it) and the King Ahriman Piece's Death (fixed here); Soulreaper's Armor is the only item that resists Doom.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.306 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- **White Mage: Temperance and Divine Caress are now handled as the two separate actions they are.** Since the pair was split, the heal combos watched for the Divine Grace buff and pressed whatever Temperance had turned into. Now Temperance itself is used when it is ready - in the single-target, area and simple heal modes and in the raidwide features alike - and Divine Caress is pressed on its own when it is ready. The area-of-effect simple heal mode gains a Divine Caress step it did not have, and the Asylum replacement mode now tries Asylum first, then Temperance, then Divine Caress, instead of preferring Temperance while Asylum was on cooldown.
- **A ground-placed action is no longer fired before it is ready.** The action watcher could send a ground-target placement for a replacement action that was still on cooldown; it now checks readiness first.
- Merges upstream WrathCombo changes through 2026-10-14 (9 commits). The automatic regen and shield checks on the focus target now use the plugin's own status lookup, ending an ambiguity with the shared library's lookup of the same name.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.305 (2026-10-15) [testing]
- **Beastmaster in the Crucible of the Unbroken, Abaddon Piece: the rotation no longer stands idle while a Morpho is alive.** The Abaddon was held back from the start of the fight until every Morpho was gone, and the Morphos themselves are never attacked, so for as long as a Morpho lived (over a minute in a recorded fight) the Abaddon was the only enemy and nothing was left that the rotation was allowed to hit: no damage and no aggro while the Morphos confused the character. Intended behaviour in this piece: the Drake and the Barbmoles are killed first, as before; once the Abaddon is the only enemy left it is attacked and chipped down to 35% of its health, and held there while any Morpho is alive, so it is never killed ahead of the Morphos it feeds on; once the last Morpho is gone it is attacked to the end. Eggs and Morphos as targets are still never attacked, and the Gigantis gel rule is unchanged.
- The Abaddon's Regen (Rehabilitation, one minute, renewed each time it eats a Morpho) is deliberately not dispelled: Quelling Wave never removed it in the recorded casts (15 casts on the Abaddon, the buff always ran its full minute), so the rotation does not spend casts on it. The Drake's Blaze Spikes are still dispelled.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.304 (2026-10-14) [testing]
- **While another plugin controls the rotation, a training dummy that is the chosen target is left alone too.** The Manual mode, the manual area-of-effect aim and the Tank Target mode take their target from a selected target - the character's own, or in Tank Target mode the tank's - instead of from the enemy filter that 1.0.4.303 added, so a Striking Dummy that was already selected could still be struck while a lease was held. The same dummy check now covers that path: while another plugin is in control or still holds a lease, the dummy is not attacked even as the chosen target; without a lease the player's own choice stands.
- The external-control check reads the lease table directly on every tick instead of building a list for each read (the rotation consults it several times a tick).
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged. Not verified in play yet.

v1.0.4.303 (2026-10-14) [testing]
- **Another plugin driving the rotation (AutoDuty and the like) no longer attacks a training dummy, and no longer keeps control after it has stopped.** A training dummy never dies, so a first hit pulled out of combat held the character in combat with it, and the rotation then went on hitting it even after external control had ended. Now, while another plugin controls the rotation or still holds a lease on it, the Striking Dummy is not picked as an enemy at all. External control also does not apply in cities, inns and housing districts or their interiors, so a plugin that walks through one cannot start a fight there. AutoDuty re-asserts the rotation every 5 seconds during a run and goes silent between runs without releasing it, so it now counts as in control for one minute after its last call instead of ten; other plugins keep the ten-minute window. Every job is covered: the checks sit in the shared auto-rotation gate, not in any job's combo.
- Testing channel only; the production channel is unchanged.
